sparse_input.generator: numpy.random.default_rng (PCG64), seeded with [seed, n, round(density_pct*1000), structure_id, matrix_id]

structures.uniform: exactly round(d*n^2) nonzeros at distinct positions drawn uniformly at random from the n^2 positions
structures.banded: exactly round(d*n^2) nonzeros in the narrowest band |i-j| <= w that holds them: diagonals |i-j| < w are full, the remaining nonzeros are placed at random positions of the two outermost diagonals

sparse_input.format: CSR1 binary: int64 header {magic, n, nnz}, int64 row_ptr[n+1], int32 col[nnz] (sorted per row), float64 val[nnz]

dense.description: Part A: baseline vs optimised dense kernels on the Assignment 1 inputs

sparse.description: Part B: CSR vs dense on matched sparse inputs (uniform random structure)

structure.description: Part B: same density, different nonzero structure (CSR only; dense time does not depend on the structure)

sparse_large.description: Part B: sizes beyond the dense budget (CSR), with the dense method attempted until it fails
